value.hook: Open before writing any daemon notice/nudge that wakes or tells seats, changing a just recipe that launches the daemon, or touching pij close / registration continuity
value.title: wildcat: idle nudge done right (F136/F144), recipe env proofs, owner-close and status-line heal (F149)

sections.name: body
sections.value:
Idle nudge (#189, #195), what reviewers forced:
- **Qualify only real in-flight work.** Count a task instance holding (`coder/224`, `reviewer/183b`, `coder/f144`; `is_task_instance`, cap `TASK_NUMBER_MAX_DIGITS`), an open plan or fix claim, or a delivered request with `answered_at` NULL. A bare long-lived role is a resting specialist (C30). F150 is pending: exclude `--reply none`.
- **Never cold-wake for a nudge.** Wake only on Clear or Busy. Unknown counts as not warm, and the prime gets an FYI instead. Audit with `receipt_label(false)`.
- **Re-check everything in the one conditional INSERT...SELECT mark.** That means the own-event anchor, the seat still idle, and the exact keys of the named work (bound as JSON, read with `json_each`). A veto sends nothing.
- **Unguessable ids.** Every notice id gets its own 16 random bytes, the nudge's and each FYI's separately. `/v1/events` publishes ids before the next hold, so a derived id can be reserved by someone else first.
- **No residual filters.** Use a partial expression index (`spine_own_events`) rather than a JSON filter that scans the idle tail. Name the index with `INDEXED BY` so drift fails loudly.

Mutation-check hygiene:
- A mutant that makes SQL unusable under `INDEXED BY` errors every call. That's an INVALID kill: check that the intended test failed, for the intended reason.
- Where two layers guard the same thing, each layer needs its own isolating test. Example: the snapshot vs the stored row, handed in as a fabricated snapshot.
- Save baselines to a file. Reviewers ask for the source commit, baseline and restore every round.

Recipes (#196):
- `crates/testkit/tests/build_stamps.rs` `run_with`/`try_run_seeded` runs a recipe body with fake git, cargo, lsof and launchctl, and reads the daemon env or the written plist.
- Normalize env values to 1/0 before writing a plist, and refuse anything else before building or killing.
- Parse the plist for real with python3 plistlib, not the fake plutil.

F149, why "closed" seats come back:
- `pij close` only tombstones.
- The Claude status line's heal loop (`harness/scripts/claude-statusline-pij.sh`, one detached adopt per 15 s on a whoami miss) re-registers the same session, and continuity used to lift the owner-close.
- Fix in flight: owner-close is terminal; the refusal puts `E-RS-SEAT-RETIRED` first in the message; the status line writes a `.closed` marker and stops healing.
- Read the store first (`sqlite3 "file:$HOME/.pij-rs/pij.sqlite?mode=ro"`; spine events per seat around the tombstone): the root cause there was not the one in the packet.

Builds: if the shared target lock starves you (F145), ask pm-001 for an own target dir, and delete it after merge.
